chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Don Byas
summary: Collins met Byas at the Three Deuces with Eddie Mallory's band, worked opposite him with Slam Stewart, and later in Holland, calling him intelligent and Hawkins-like.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I met Don, here we go again, in Chicago, at the Three Duces. He came through with Eddy Mallory's band, and Ethel Waters, and I think Tyree Glenn was with the

same band. This is the first time I'd ever met him, but he was a genius, you know. So while they were in town they would come down every night, and blow. Okay. So I -- when I went to New York of course on the street I worked opposite him all the time, because I was with Slam Stewart, and we worked the Three Deuces. And as I told you, the man who -- his name was Sammy Kaye, he owned the Three Deuces, he managed Slam so that was our headquarters. We could stay there forever. But we would go out occasionally, but we would always come back to the Three Deuces. So consequently we worked opposite all the attractions, which included Art, Don Byas, and Don was a very intelligent guy, you know. He was kind of a little different, you know.

Well, I mean, he had an awful lot of class, too, you know. He was a very intelligent guy, musical-ly and otherwise, you know. And he reminded me -- I think Don's style was more like the sound of Coleman Hawkins too. Well, Coleman was a big influence as you know, on most saxophone, other than Lester. Lester had his following also, you know. But Don was more like Coleman Hawkins, I think, and so it was just a pleasure, to have worked opposite, not with him. I didn't play with him but opposite him.
And right after then he went to Europe, and stayed, see. So he worked opposite us again in Holland, and around
'60 something. He was living in Holland at this -- (inaudible).
Yeah, yeah. He was living there then. But as I say it was just -- by working there I got a chance to work opposite all of the -- everybody, you know, all of the greats.
